# Moth People
Moth people are a winged species, sporting antennae and similar bug-like features.
## Background
One would never have expected a simple moth escaping the confines of Earth to evolve into the beings they are today.
Once creatures of the night, now your kind roam the endless expanse of space, guided by curiosity and instinct alike. Though still often dismissed as mere light-chasers or fabric-munchers, those who underestimate them quickly learn that beneath their familiar insectoid forms lies a species of adaptability.
Unlike many other races, they claim no single homeworld (or, more likely, they forgot where it was). Instead, they have a vast, shimmering network of ships collectively known as the Fleet. Some say their approach to the Fleet echoes human militarism, a careful and sometimes xenophobic strategy to protect the swarm from external threats.
The Fleet is the cradle of moth society, the place where most are raised to learn the ways of navigation, survival, and interstellar diplomacy. But many flutter away from the Fleet, exploring new systems or seeking quieter lives far from the Fleet’s ordered routines. Some find fame as traders, explorers, or guardians, while others choose solitude among the stars, following instinct more than ambition.
## Unique Abilities
### Winged Dash
- Moth people can [color=#1e90ff]dash small distances once in 6.5 seconds[/color] using their wings, but that requires the gravity to be present.
## Diet
- They can eat cotton, fabrics and clothing, but virtually none of the food that others would consider "edible".
## Benefits
- They take [color=#1e90ff]30% less Cold damage[/color] - Their wings give them better acceleration if there is no gravity on the station, but they still can't move without equipment when floating out in space. - They are also [color=#1e90ff]6.5% lighter than most species.[/color]
## Drawbacks
- They move [color=#ffa500]6.5% slower[/color] than other species due to their weak legs. - They take [color=#ffa500]30% more Heat and 6.5% more Brute damage, and catch on fire more easily[/color]. - They prefer a somewhat lower temperature range than humans, making them more susceptible to higher temperatures.
